label: Lakes of the Basin of Mexico (modelled, experimental)
summary: The five lakes of the Basin of Mexico (Zumpango, Xaltocan, Texcoco, Xochimilco, Chalco) before the colonial drainage: the basin-connected 2270 m contour of a smoothed modern DEM, calibrated to the lakes' area, 4 ka BP to 1600 CE, modelled; Tenochtitlan's island is kept dry; only the southern lakes count as fresh water.
datum: metres above the geoid on Terrarium zoom 6 averaged to 2.5' (smoothed: the level is calibrated to area on this surface, not the lakes' surveyed ~2236-2240 m)

epochs.name: before the drainage
epochs.state: the lakes at their calibrated level, held through the window; seasonal and yearly swings not modelled
epochs.water: brackish to saline (Texcoco, Xaltocan, Zumpango); fresh (Xochimilco, Chalco): only the southern lakes give fresh water

mask.grid: 8640 x 4320 world pixels of 2.5'; x0, y0 = column, row of the patch's north-west pixel (row 0 north, column 0 180 W)

distance.grid: 4320 x 2160 HYDE 5' cells; x0, y0 = column, row of the patch's north-west cell
distance.encoding: water_distance.json: metres = max_metres * (code / 255) ** 2, code 0 = water in the cell
distance.rule: min(static distance image, distance to the lake cells south of 19.34 N); outside the patch the static image is exact

outside_epochs: scenario inactive: the geography is unknown at that date, which is not the same as a dry basin; the app draws and places as it does without the flag

area_reference_km2.source: the lake system's area at contact as usually given (about 1,000-2,000 km2, varying with season and year; e.g. Sanders, Parsons & Santley 1979, The Basin of Mexico)

licence: derived from AWS Terrarium elevation tiles (public-domain and openly licensed DEMs, attribution per the tiles' notice)

sources.height: AWS Terrarium elevation tiles, zoom 6, mean of 3 x 3 samples per 2.5' pixel (as site_terrain.py)
sources.level: calibrated: the lowest level at which the fill reaches all five lakes, checked against the lakes' usual area; the surveyed lake surface was ~2236-2240 m
sources.chronology: lakes present through the Holocene; held from 4 ka BP (Formative shore villages) to 1600 CE, before the Desagüe of Huehuetoca begun in 1607
sources.freshwater: Texcoco saline, Xochimilco and Chalco fresh (spring-fed), Zumpango and Xaltocan brackish; Nezahualcoyotl's dike (~1449) separated fresh from salt water in the western lake

uncertainty: The shoreline is a contour of a 2.4 km DEM averaged to 4.6 km, calibrated to area: the shape is the basin floor's, not a mapped shore.
The lakes rose and fell with the seasons and the years; one level is held for 3,650 years.
Only Tenochtitlan and Tlatelolco are kept dry; other islands (Xaltocan, Mixquic), the causeways and the chinampas are not modelled.
Which parts were fresh is simplified to a latitude line south of the city.
Nothing is said before 4 ka BP or after 1600: not dry, not wet.

terrain.path: /terrain/pastwater/earth_{year}.webp (terrain_image.py --pastwater); other years use the ordinary images
